translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital he ordered Li Chongjin to hold the siege; Renshan again seized an opening and stormed our southern camp.

sentences.zh: 自是圍之愈急，城中饑死者甚眾。

translations.literal: From then the siege grew tighter; inside the city very many died of hunger.
translations.idiomatic: From then the siege grew tighter and very many inside the city died of hunger.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，淮寇復來救援，列寨於紫金山，夾道相屬，累然數十里，垂及壽壁，而重進兵幾不能支，世宗患之，遂復議親征。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year Huai rebels came again to relieve the siege, forming camps at Zijin Mountain in a continuous line along the road for several tens of li, nearly reaching the walls of Shou while Chongjin's army could hardly hold; Shizong was troubled and debated campaigning in person again.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year three Huai rebels came to relieve the siege, forming camps at Zijin Mountain in a line along the road for tens of li, nearly reaching the walls of Shou while Chongjin's army could hardly hold; Shizong was troubled and debated campaigning in person again.

sentences.zh: 車駕至壽春，命今上率師破紫金山之眾，擒其應援使陳承昭以獻。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage reached Shouchun he ordered the present emperor to lead troops to break the host at Zijin Mountain and capture their relief commander Chen Chengzhao to present.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage reached Shouchun he ordered the present emperor to lead troops to break the host at Zijin Mountain and capture relief commander Chen Chengzhao to present.

sentences.zh: 仁贍聞援兵既敗，計無所出，但扼腕浩嘆而已。

translations.literal: When Renshan heard the relief army had been defeated he had no plan left and could only wring his wrists and sigh greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Renshan heard the relief army was defeated he had no plan left and could only wring his wrists and sigh.

sentences.zh: 會世宗以紫金山之捷，飛詔以諭之，時仁贍臥疾已亟，因翻然納款，而城內諸軍萬計，皆屏息以聽其命。

translations.literal: When Shizong, on the victory at Zijin Mountain, sent a flying edict to instruct him, Renshan was already gravely ill in bed; he therefore suddenly submitted, and the troops in the city numbering in the tens of thousands all held their breath and obeyed his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong sent a flying edict on the Zijin Mountain victory to instruct him, Renshan was already gravely ill; he suddenly submitted, and the tens of thousands of troops in the city all held their breath and obeyed his command.

sentences.zh: 及見於行在，世宗撫之甚厚，賜與加等，復令入城養病，尋授天平軍節度使、兼中書令。

translations.literal: When he was received at headquarters Shizong treated him very generously, gave him gifts of higher grade, and again ordered him into the city to nurse his illness; soon he was appointed military governor of Tianping and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received at headquarters Shizong treated him very generously, gave him higher gifts, and again ordered him into the city to recover; soon he was appointed military governor of Tianping and concurrently Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 制出之日，薨於其家，年五十八。

translations.literal: On the day the appointment was issued he died at his home, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: On the day the appointment was issued he died at home, aged fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，遣使吊祭，命內臣監護喪事，追封彭城郡王。

translations.literal: When Shizong heard he sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, ordered inner attendants to supervise the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong heard he sent envoys to mourn, ordered inner attendants to supervise the funeral, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 後以其子崇讃為懷州刺史。

translations.literal: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Later his son Chongzan was made prefect of Huai.

sentences.zh: 仁贍輕財重士，法令嚴肅，重圍之中，其子崇諫犯軍禁，即令斬之，故能以一城之眾，連年拒守。

translations.literal: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military prohibition and he at once ordered him beheaded—therefore with the troops of one city he could hold out for years.
translations.idiomatic: Renshan was light with wealth and heavy toward scholars; his laws were stern; in the tight siege his son Chongjian violated military law and he at once had him beheaded—therefore with one city's troops he could hold out for years.

sentences.zh: 逮其來降，而其下未敢竊議者，保其後嗣，抑有由焉。

translations.literal: When he came to surrender his subordinates did not dare whisper in private—he secured his descendants, and there was reason for that.
translations.idiomatic: When he surrendered his subordinates did not dare whisper in private—he had secured his descendants, and there was reason in that.

sentences.zh: 崇贊仕周，累為郡守。

translations.literal: Chongzan served Zhou and successively held prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzan served Zhou and successively governed prefectures.

sentences.zh: 幼子崇諒，後自江南歸於本朝，亦位至省郎。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chongliang later returned from Jiangnan to the court and also rose to a post in the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chongliang later returned from Jiangnan to the court and also rose to a secretariat post.
